info.title: Rui Host
info.description:
The Rui Host's local protocol: HTTP/1.1 over the Unix socket of a running Host, one POST per request, generated from the Host's own wire types.

Request bodies list their fields in the order this document lists them; the Host refuses another order. Numbers that may exceed 2^53 travel as decimal strings. String bounds are in UTF-8 bytes (`x-rui-max-bytes`).

post.summary: The Host's identity, capacity and provider routes. Also the readiness probe.
Stops the Host, or with drain_seconds holds new Turns and stops once running work ends or the bound passes.
Holds every new Turn while paused, or releases them. Running work continues.
Creates or reconfigures a Session. Retried by its key.

409.description: The key was used before with different input (the conflict reply), or the request names another Store or Host instance (a refusal).

post.summary: Sends a Message to a Session, or creates the Session when `session` is empty. Retried by its key. Each `/name` word in the text that names a skill in the recipient's catalog appends that skill to what the model reads; the text is saved as written. Only an empty `session` carries (and requires) `configuration`; `require_model` refuses the Message unless the Session's provider, or the new Session's, is served. The body starts with the client environment, `X-Rui-Environment-Bytes` long, before the JSON.

409.description: The key was used before with different input (the conflict reply), or the request names another Store or Host instance (a refusal).

post.summary: Publishes one value from the running Action identified by its sender handle.
Reads one Session-owned Action's status and one bounded final-result window without waiting or consuming it.
What became of the command sent with this key.
The answer text of the Message sent with this key.

A Session's report, or one failed provider response.

200.description: The Session report, or, for a failed response export, that response's bytes.

post.summary: One page of Sessions, newest first, or what changed since a token. `through` and `after_reference` appear together, only with `since`; token reads start with zero `after` and `ceiling`. `window` reads one page of Archived Sessions, newest archive first, in one round: only with `archive` = `archived`, no `workspace`, no `since`, and zero `after` and `ceiling`.
One page of a Session's conversation, newest first.
The content of one conversation item.

200.description: The content bytes, from the requested offset.

post.summary: The complete certified, ordered part list of a Message or Action Resolution parts value, addressed by its owner in the Session.
The exact bytes of one part of an owner's parts value, framed as conversation content.

200.description: The content bytes, from the requested offset.

post.summary: Search public Session activity newest first with bounded snippets.
One page of a Session's activity feed, with its work and queue at the page's boundary.
The content of one activity row.

200.description: The content bytes, from the requested offset.

post.summary: Bounded skill metadata from a Session catalog or prospective Workspace discovery.
The models each served connection offers.
Asks the Host to list one MCP server, or every configured server, again. Each reply names the generation asked; tools-status reports when it has landed.
Each configured MCP server's list state, last outcome, finished generation and tool count.

anyOf.description: One resolved model Operation at its admission position. Timings describe the FINAL attempt only: latency_ms is request sent to resolution; first_event_ms is request sent to the first HTTP response event (including an interim head), not the first token. Missing evidence, usage or timings is null. A resolution may become visible within a previously captured end (D219).
